callback_lifetime.ownership: The callback object and event handle are module globals in one private child.
callback_lifetime.termination: The child uses os._exit after flushed output; process termination owns event cleanup and avoids Python interpreter teardown while a control-handler thread may enter it.
callback_lifetime.mode_error: null when GetConsoleMode succeeds; captured immediately on failure.
callback_lifetime.wait_error: Captured immediately only when WaitForSingleObject returns WAIT_FAILED (0xffffffff); WAIT_TIMEOUT is a distinct observation.

observation_limits: Preserve describes state after CPython and CRT startup; it does not establish the raw inherited ignore attribute.
A difference between the two Python children does not prove the original PowerShell/ping failure has the same cause.
The child begins a bounded 1500 ms observation after printing readiness; transport and scheduling latency can consume that interval.
No observed control event is not proof that delivery could never occur.
Both routes and their errors remain reported; their measurements do not replace the original PowerShell success assertion.

standalone_linux_pty_echo_proof.scope: Two owned, pipe-gated subprocesses; original echo contains marker before execution, split echo does not, and both execute to the same marker. Not a Rust or macOS result.
